plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above my value risks losing money, and bidding below my value risks losing profitable wins. With a value of $11, the optimal action is to bid exactly $11, ensuring I maximize expected profit without unnecessary risk.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with 3 bidders and independent private values. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy—you pay the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you win), so shading your bid only risks losing profitable wins without reducing what you pay. Since my value is $34, I will bid exactly $34 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy: since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own), there's no incentive to shade the bid. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks winning at a loss. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, and this being the only round, the optimal strategy is straightforward: bid exactly my private value of $42 to maximize expected profit.
